Theme

Latin word

praemium

praemium, praemiī n.

noun, second declension

a prize, a reward; a reward

In this lexicon

  • award

    the recommended word · classical · Verg. A. 5.70: praemia palmae; Gell. 18.2.3; Traupman 365

  • reward

    the recommended word · classical · Quint. 1.1.20; Ter. Eun. 5.8.27: dōnum et praemium (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • cūnctī adsint meritaeque exspectent praemia palmae

    let everyone be there and wait for the prizes they have earnedVerg. A. 5.70

    In the entry for award

  • praemium solvendae quaestiōnis pōnēbat librum veteris scrīptōris vel Graecum vel Latīnum et corōnam ē laurō plexam

    as the prize for solving a question he offered a book by an old writer, Greek or Latin, and a crown woven of bayGell. 18.2.3

    In the entry for award

  • Nescītis quod iī quī in stadiō currunt, omnēs quidem currunt, sed ūnus accipit bravium?

    Do you not know that those who run in the stadium all run, but one receives the prize?Vulg. 1 Cor. 9.24

    In the entry for award

  • praemiīs etiam, quae capit illa aetās, ēvocētur

    let him be coaxed on, too, with rewards such as that age enjoysQuint. 1.1.20

    In the entry for reward

  • ingrāta es, inquit, ōre quae nostrō caput incolume abstulerīs et mercēdem postulēs

    “You are ungrateful,” he said, “to have taken your head safe out of my mouth and then ask for a reward”Phaedr. 1.8.11–12
